status: Confirmed renderer-wide WebGL canvas alpha defect; live source unchanged
cause: Browser default WebGL2 chooses LegacyGL. GLState::blendFunc calls glBlendFunc(SRC_ALPHA, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA), applying the source alpha factor to stored framebuffer alpha. Over opaque background, glyph coverage a leaves output alpha a*a+(1-a), causing browser premultiplied canvas compositing to add CSS page background through missing coverage a*(1-a).
competing_hypotheses: Exact-coordinate model error below1 channel value mean for Latin/Bengali/icons excludes positioning, Bengali shaping and gamma as the main cause. Earlier alpha-squared coverage observation is explained by lost framebuffer alpha, not proven premultiplied upload.
guard: GLOB2_WEBGL2 only; desktop GL entry points and existing RGB factors unchanged. All current wrapper calls use source SRC_ALPHA or ONE and destination ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA.
b34_overlap: git diff7f..b34 confirms no changes to GraphicContext.cpp, GraphicContextCompound.cpp, DrawableSurface.cpp, RenderDevice.cpp, presentation-surface.js or shader generator. Upstream TrueTypeFont change only opts nb into authored advances, independent from defect.
regression: Use actual fresh browser settings UI at viewport1280x900/DPR1. Compare fixed opaque navigation crop after changing ONLY canvas CSS background black→white; any RGB change reveals false framebuffer alpha. Current captures analytically imply up to~64channel difference at50percent coverage; after correction require maxdiff<=2. Run same check with software control, both serial/threaded WebGL2, and compare final Bengali/Latin/icon contrast against software. Restore CSS in finally; retain PNGs, exact producer hashes and measured differences.
pending: Patch must be applied after clean b34 integration, followed by fresh browser rebuild and actual pixel/visual recheck. No pass claim from source inspection or token assertions.
